All 12 BPMN files carry a DI layout (`bpmndi:BPMNDiagram`; M-010b, 2026-11-12), generated by packgen
   (`tools/packgen/compliance.py`), and route their user tasks to seats (M-010c, below).

- **Seat routing (M-010c, in progress).** The 12 BPMN files now have their DI layout (M-010b), but their user tasks
  still use candidate groups (for example `DPO`), not seat routing; the seat routing is being designed and coded under
  M-010c.
- **Seat routing (M-010c), coded 2026-11-12, tests not run.** Every user task of the 12 processes is routed to a seat
  variable passed at process start (`candidateGroups="${dpoSeat}"`), never to a role code. The seat of each role is
  configuration, with no pack, region or role default: `sangam.compliance.seats.<ROLE>`, or per tenant
  `sangam.compliance.tenant.<tenant>.seats.<ROLE>` (`ComplianceConfig.seat`; the role code as written, else in lower
  case, which is the form a single-word environment variable such as `SANGAM_COMPLIANCE_SEATS_DPO` binds to). A start
  that needs a missing seat is refused with **409 `INVALID_STATE`** naming every missing property, before anything is
  written (fail closed; no fallback to the role). Variable names: `DPO` → `dpoSeat`, `CISO-HEAD` → `cisoHeadSeat`.

  | Process | Roles (seat variables) | Started by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `sangam-dsr-access`, `-rectification`, `-nomination`, `-automated-decision`, `-objection` | `DPO` | `DataSubjectRightsService` |
  | `sangam-dsr-erasure` | `RECORDS-OFFICER` | `DataSubjectRightsService` |
  | `sangam-dsr-grievance` | `GRIEVANCE-OFFICER`, `DPO` | `DataSubjectRightsService` |
  | `sangam-dsr-accounting`, `sangam-dsr-restriction` | `PRIVACY-OFFICER` | `DataSubjectRightsService` |
  | `sangam-breach-incident` | `DPO`, `CISO` | `BreachIncidentService.register` |
  | `sangam-incident-report` | `CISO`, `CISO-HEAD` | `IncidentReportingService` (also checked by a breach registration that links an incident) |
  | `sangam-breach-notification-plan` | `PRIVACY-OFFICER` | `BreachNotificationPlanner.start`, once, right after the breach is registered, and only where the tenant's jurisdiction defines breach notification rules or risk factors (`BreachNotificationPlanner.applies`; owner decision 2026-11-12: for example EU-GDPR and US-HIPAA; IN keeps its fixed-step flow and needs no `PRIVACY-OFFICER` seat) |
